blocking.issue: The round-trip test asserts a count that contradicts pack section 8.7 rule 3 and the ADR's own Keys row. Rule 3 says consumptive calls run as one script when their keys share a hash slot. The Keys row says the `{<SHA-256 of the key value>}` hash tag lets them share one script. So two `ratelimit` Policies with the same key value on one Route (for example `ratelimit-global` and `ratelimit-orders` in the Configuration model example) make one call between them, not one each. A conforming implementation would fail the test as written.
blocking.evidence: Line 98: "- **Round-trip test**, Planned (M1): a counting State Store proxy asserts zero commands for local denials and exactly one per admitted request per Policy." Line 54 (Keys row): "the hash tag lets consumptive calls share one script (pack section 8.7 rule 3)". Pack 8.7 rule 3: "one script when their keys share a hash slot, otherwise sequential round trips".
blocking.fix: Rewrite as: "- **Round-trip test**, Planned (M1): a counting State Store proxy asserts zero commands for local denials and over-limit cache hits, at most one blocking call per admitted request per Policy, and one shared script when consumptive keys share a hash slot (pack section 8.7 rules 1 and 3)."

blocking.issue: The ADR says the chosen option shields shards and lists hot-key protection as a driver. Its Consequences never say that a key spread across many Nodes, such as a busy service limit, still saturates its shard. The owning document's Failure matrix gives the saturation outcome, and Scalability and distributed state adds a MUST for `localOnly` mode above about 25,000 `requests` per second (hypothesis). By omitting both, the ADR claims more than its owning documents and hides the main open dependency (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1 (c)).

Compare docs/architecture/09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md, Failure matrix: "| Hot constant key saturates a shard | `ratelimit`; co-tenant keys | Up to N × ceiling calls per window; above about 100,000 per second (hypothesis) every Node's shard breaker opens and co-tenants apply `failureMode` |". Compare docs/architecture/11-scalability-and-distributed-state.md line 294: "A key whose `requests` exceed 25% of one shard's calls, about 25,000 per second (hypothesis), MUST use `localOnly` mode, option (c) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1".

The owning document assumes about 100,000 calls per second per shard (hypothesis), so a key spread over many Nodes with more than about 25,000 `requests` per second saturates its shard and co-tenants apply `failureMode`, until `localOnly` mode (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1) exists."

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Per-Node ceiling and State Store failure rows; Figure 1)
blocking.issue: The ADR says fail-open admits "within the local buckets", with the full limit as the ceiling when a Node has no declared ceiling and no count. The owning document and Scalability and distributed state clamp the buckets while GCRA fails. Derived ceilings drop to the unfloored max(1, 2 × `requests` / N_published) per aligned window. A Control-mode Node without a count, whose normal ceiling is the full limit, drops to max(1, `requests` / 100). Read literally, the ADR lets a Control-mode Node without a count fail open at the full limit, so N_countless Nodes admit N_countless × limit. The owning document admits N_countless × max(1, `requests` / 100). This contradicts the owning document's Failure matrix row and the bounds table.
